name: TensorFold
cost: Not stated in the README (model weights have their own licenses)
works_with: Macs with Apple Silicon, Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, Windows with an NVIDIA GPU (build guide)
short: Runs open language models on your own Mac or NVIDIA machine from a single Zig binary, with an OpenAI-style API and no Python needed.
what: TensorFold is an inference engine written in Zig. It reads model checkpoints and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly, so serving needs no Python or MLX. It serves chat completions, completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages on a local port. There is also a small local web app and a beta Mac app.
who: Developers who want to serve local models on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA hardware. Skip it if you have neither, and check each model's memory needs first: many models in its table need a big Mac or a GB10.
needs: A Mac with Apple Silicon and Homebrew, or
Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0)
Disk space for the model you pull

steps.title: Install on a Mac and start a small model
steps.code:
brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold
tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3
tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking

steps.title: Or install on Linux with NVIDIA
steps.text: This downloads the release archive, checks its checksum and serves the same model.
steps.code:
V=1.2.7
case "$(uname -m)" in
  aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;;
  x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;;
  *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256"
tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz"
export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH"
tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; }
tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3
tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking

steps.title: Send a request
steps.text: Leave the server running and use another terminal.
steps.code:
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}'

steps.title: Check a bigger model first
steps.text: `tensorfold info REPO` reports a checkpoint's memory floor before you serve it.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Serve Qwen3.5-2B as `local-model` and send it "Say hello in one sentence." with the curl command above.

watch: Model weights have their own licenses.
The Linux build refuses NVIDIA drivers older than R580.
Context, parallel requests, prompt caches and drafters need memory beyond the weights, and many listed models have no published RAM minimum.
`tensorfold web` can offer to install the web app with `uv`, and asks first.
